subject: Using Seewave for Synthesized Music Data in Shiny Apps

messages.author: 2de6ce7afa3681ac
messages.subject: Using Seewave for Synthesized Music Data in Shiny Apps
parts:
Hi All, 

 
Can anyone point me to resources / ideas using Seewave and Shiny to build things like simple interactive music synthesizers and sequencers?

I wanted to create something similar to the following
https://youtu.be/P9xebSuW9ys?t=139

Originally I built this software using React, D3.js and Tone.js but am currently rebuilding it all in Shiny - so far its much easier (Shiny and R are great to work with!) but has left me with the challenge of how to manage audio. 

Specifically, I am interested in the following types of requirements:
  • Allowing users to treat the app like a music synth, and adjust parameters in the Shiny App, like filters and wave types
  • Having multiple voices/frequencies sounding at the same time (last time I checked tone.js was limited in this)
  • Playing time series music data (so if I construct a list of frequencies, durations and locations from a musicxml or midi file, I can play a synthesised version from a specific point)
  • Playing actual audio files (so as well as being able to play synthesised data, I could play an audio recording of the music from a specific point. 
  • Being able to adjust the speed of audio in a shiny app. 
I know this is a bit of a big list of requirements, but any general ideas / starting points would be greatly appreciated, or if there are related projects that people are working on. 

My fall back option with was just managing it through Tone.js and external Javascript files held with the Shiny App, but  this makes the code much more messy and I would love to manage this kind of thing in R. 

Thanks (and thanks for creating this great library!)

messages.author: cee31d592db1da75
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Using Seewave for Synthesized Music Data in Shiny Apps
parts:
You might find this Shiny widget interesting even though it is pretty much what
you noted that you don't want.
https://thomaslevine.com/scm/bradio/dir?ci=tip

The hard part for me is always getting around R not really being concurrent.
One way to get around that is to render the music in JavaScript, and another is
to render it in C.

A while ago I started writing an audio driver for R (sndio because I use
OpenBSD) and never finished. My idea was to make it loop over a sound until you
switch the cache to another sound.

I haven't synthesized music through Seewave, alas.

I love all of these initiatives. I dream that one day we will have a music track
at UseR! rather than merely an IDE falsely advertised as a "studio".
